issues.legal_issue: An arbitration clause contained in an insufficiently stamped instrument cannot be acted upon to appoint an arbitrator unless the required stamp duty and penalty are paid.
material_facts: The arbitration clause was contained in a lease deed that was chargeable with stamp duty but was insufficiently stamped.
The High Court Registrar (Judicial) determined the deficit stamp duty and penalty and directed payment.
The parties seeking arbitration did not pay the determined deficit duty and penalty.
The High Court nevertheless relied on the lease deed to appoint an arbitrator on their application.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not rely on the lease deed or its arbitration clause while the instrument remained insufficiently stamped and the required duty and penalty remained unpaid. The appointment order was set aside and the arbitration application was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 33 and 34 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, a court must examine a chargeable instrument produced before it and, if it is not duly stamped, impound it; the instrument cannot be admitted in evidence or acted upon unless the applicable duty and penalty are paid. Applying SMS Tea Estates Private Limited v. Chandmari Tea Company Private Limited, (2011) 14 SCC 66, the Court held that this bar also prevents a court from acting on an arbitration clause contained in the instrument. The analogous provisions considered in SMS Tea Estates were Sections 33 and 35 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899; the instrument may be acted upon after the duty and penalty are paid in the manner provided by the applicable stamp law.

rule.if: arbitration_appointment_application and arbitration_clause_in_chargeable_instrument and instrument_insufficiently_stamped and stamp_deficit_unpaid

predicates.arbitration_appointment_application: A party applied for appointment of an arbitrator to resolve a dispute.
predicates.arbitration_clause_in_chargeable_instrum: The arbitration clause was contained in an instrument chargeable with stamp duty.
predicates.instrument_insufficiently_stamped: The instrument did not bear the stamp duty required for it.
predicates.stamp_deficit_unpaid: The party relying on the instrument had not paid the required deficit duty and penalty.

issues.definition: When an arbitration appointment application relies on an arbitration clause in a chargeable instrument that is insufficiently stamped and the required deficit remains unpaid, the clause cannot be acted upon.

issues.legal_issue: A party that delays seeking arbitration after participating in court proceedings, takes inconsistent positions about the relied-on instrument, and fails to substantiate its account of when contractual performance could begin is not entitled to equitable relief on that basis.
material_facts: The parties seeking arbitration participated in the opposing parties’ injunction suit for about two years and three months before applying for appointment of an arbitrator.
They did not seek referral to arbitration in that suit at the earliest opportunity.
In the suit, they treated the document as a lease deed, but in the appointment proceedings they described it as an agreement to develop the property after tenants were evicted.

The lease deed stated that its term began when it was signed, assigned responsibility for obtaining vacant possession and building-plan sanctions to the lessee, and provided that tenant litigation would not affect the agreed lease term.
Apart from a bald statement that the last tenant was evicted in 2010, they produced no supporting material for that claim.
issues.conclusion: The Court found that the parties seeking arbitration were not entitled to relief on equitable grounds and that their claim that the agreement was to be registered only after the tenants were evicted and building plans were sanctioned was unsupported by the lease terms.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the parties’ conduct and the express terms of the lease deed. It relied on the deed’s commencement term, its allocation of responsibility for securing vacant possession and building-plan sanctions, and its provision that tenant litigation would not affect the lease term. The Court also considered the delay in seeking arbitration, participation in the suit without seeking an early referral, inconsistent descriptions of the document, and the lack of evidence supporting the asserted timing of eviction. No earlier case was cited for this equitable assessment.

rule.if: arbitration_appointment_application and prolonged_court_proceeding_participation and no_early_arbitration_referral and inconsistent_instrument_characterization and unsupported_performance_timing_claim

predicates.arbitration_appointment_application: A party applied for appointment of an arbitrator to resolve a dispute.
predicates.prolonged_court_proceeding_participation: The party seeking arbitration participated in the opposing party’s court proceeding for a substantial period before applying for arbitration.
predicates.no_early_arbitration_referral: The party did not seek referral to arbitration in the court proceeding at the earliest opportunity.
predicates.inconsistent_instrument_characterization: The party described the relied-on instrument differently in the court proceeding and the arbitration appointment proceeding.
predicates.unsupported_performance_timing_claim: The party claimed that contractual performance or formalization depended on a later event but produced no supporting evidence, and the instrument’s terms did not support that claim.

issues.definition: When a party applies for arbitration after prolonged court participation without seeking an early referral, while taking inconsistent positions about the instrument and making an unsupported claim about when performance could begin, equitable relief is denied.
